chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh) said: Safwan narrated to them from Ibn Muskān from Abū Baṣīr from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

“The Sa’ibah (freed slave who has no heirs) has no heir; if he has a wali (heir/relative), his inheritance belongs to him and his debt is upon him. And if he has no wali, he belongs to the closest person to his master who freed him.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is not acted upon because all other reports have come stating that whenever the Sa’ibah has no wali, his inheritance belongs to the Treasury of the Muslims. We have fully detailed what is in this regard in the Book of Manumission, and we have cited in this what is sufficient, and praise be to God, and that which clarifies this further is what he narrated:

key_terms.السَّائِبَةُ: A freed slave who has no children or close relatives to inherit from him.
key_terms.بَيْتُ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The Treasury of the Muslims, representing the public fund of the Islamic state.
key_terms.وَلِيٌّ: Heir or guardian/relative entitled to inheritance.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the inheritance of a freed slave (Sa'ibah) who has no heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the inheritance of a *Sa’ibah* (freed slave with no kin), presenting a view where the patron inherits if he acts as *wali*, otherwise the closest relative of the patron inherits. Shaykh al-Tusi notes this specific narration is not the prevailing legal ruling (*ghayr ma'mul bihi*), as other traditions establish that the estate ultimately reverts to the *Bayt al-Mal* (Muslim Treasury) when no specific heir is designated. This highlights the scholarly distinction between isolated narrations and the consolidated fiqh position regarding the fiscal rights of the community in the absence of direct heirs.
